strings.name: Lip-Bu Tan
strings.summary: Lip-Bu Tan combines semiconductor investing with corporate management. He founded Walden International, backed chip startups and led electronic-design-automation company Cadence from 2009 to 2021. He became Intel CEO in 2025, overseeing transformation across products, manufacturing and foundry services. His career connects Asian and US technology ecosystems; Intel's restructuring remains subject to business results and industry risks, rather than a completed turnaround.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Participates in semiconductor-design software and technology investment, advancing the chip-startup ecosystem and electronic-design-automation industry.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Physics bachelor's, Nanyang University, Singapore; nuclear-engineering master's, MIT; MBA, University of San Francisco
strings.highlights.h1.title: Managing electronic-design software
strings.highlights.h1.text: He led Cadence through customer-focused product and organizational changes; chip-design tools are collective industry and team achievements.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cross-regional chip investment
strings.highlights.h2.text: Through Walden International and other firms, he backs semiconductor startups and connects technical talent, capital and global customers.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Intel third-quarter 2026 results
strings.timeline.t1.text: Intel reported $16.5 billion quarterly revenue, up 21%. Tan stressed increasing CPU supply while noting near-term PC-market pressure.
strings.timeline.t2.title: US government equity agreement
strings.timeline.t2.text: Intel announced an $8.9 billion agreement for an approximately 9.9% US government stake. He stayed after Trump had demanded his resignation over China-investment ties.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becoming Intel CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: The appointment announced on March 12 took effect, and he rejoined the board, succeeding two interim co-CEOs.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Cadence executive-chair tenure ends
strings.timeline.t4.text: He left the board he had joined in 2004, concluding distinct phases of executive and board service.
strings.timeline.t5.title: SIA Noyce Award
strings.timeline.t5.text: The Semiconductor Industry Association honored his longstanding contribution to semiconductors and their entrepreneurial ecosystem.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Cadence leadership transition
strings.timeline.t6.text: He handed the CEO role to Anirudh Devgan and became executive chairman, serving until 2023.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Cadence CEO
strings.timeline.t7.text: He took charge during restructuring and worked to change business execution and product direction.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founding Walden International
strings.timeline.t8.text: He established the venture-capital firm, increasingly focusing on semiconductors and related technology companies.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Nanyang physics degree
strings.timeline.t9.text: He completed his Singapore undergraduate education before studying nuclear engineering and business administration in the United States.
